evals.prompt: create a ticket for adding dark mode to the BudgetWise UI. It should toggle between light and dark themes and remember the user's preference.
evals.expected_output: A complete ticket markdown file saved to d:\repositories\budgetwise\tickets\ with the next sequential number. Must include: metadata block (Phase, Priority, Depends on, Blocks), a 'Wiki pages touched' section citing the relevant frontend wiki pages as [[wikilinks]], Objective, Frontend Changes with Angular Material theming code, Implementation Notes, Files to Create/Modify, and at least 5 Acceptance Criteria. PROJECT-STATUS.md should be updated with the new ticket entry. The skill should read wiki/index.md and relevant frontend wiki pages before drafting — not scan budgetwise-ui/src/.
expectations: Ticket file is written to d:\repositories\budgetwise\tickets\ with the next sequential number (derived from the actual tickets/ directory, not hardcoded)
Ticket contains a metadata block with Phase, Priority, Depends on, and Blocks fields
Ticket contains a 'Wiki pages touched' section with at least one [[wikilink]] to a frontend wiki page
Ticket contains an Objective section describing the dark mode feature
Ticket contains Angular/TypeScript code snippets showing how to implement theming
Ticket contains at least 5 Acceptance Criteria formatted as - [ ] checkboxes
Ticket mentions localStorage (or equivalent) for persisting the theme preference
PROJECT-STATUS.md is updated with a reference to the new ticket
The skill reads wiki/index.md and at least one frontend wiki page before drafting (no raw source scanning as the primary context source)

evals.prompt: I want to add CSV export for transactions. Users should be able to click a button on the Transactions page to download all their transactions as a CSV file. Create a ticket for this.
evals.expected_output: A complete ticket for CSV export. Should include metadata, 'Wiki pages touched' citing the transactions wiki pages, objective, frontend changes (button + download logic), and acceptance criteria. Should be frontend-only (client-side CSV generation) and must reference the existing transactions service by the name documented in the wiki — not a guessed file path.
expectations: Ticket file is written with correct sequential numbering derived from the tickets/ directory
Ticket contains a metadata block with Phase, Priority, Depends on, and Blocks fields
Ticket contains a 'Wiki pages touched' section citing [[modules/frontend/transactions]] (or the actual transactions page name in the wiki) and [[entities/transaction]]
Ticket references the existing transactions service by its real class name (as documented in the wiki) rather than creating a new one
Ticket includes TypeScript code showing how to generate and download a CSV file
Ticket specifies what columns should appear in the CSV output
Ticket contains Acceptance Criteria with at least one criterion about the downloaded file format
Ticket correctly identifies this as frontend-only work

evals.prompt: create a ticket for bulk-importing transactions from a CSV file. Users upload a CSV on the transactions page, see a preview, then confirm to import. Needs backend parsing + frontend UI.
evals.expected_output: A complete full-stack ticket. Must include Backend Changes (DTO, service method, controller endpoint), Frontend Changes (upload + preview UI), 'Wiki pages touched' citing both backend and frontend transaction wiki pages, and Implementation Notes warning about the existing atomic balance-sync pattern (Prisma $transaction) in the transactions service.
expectations: Ticket file is written with correct sequential numbering
Ticket contains both Backend Changes and Frontend Changes sections
Ticket contains a 'Wiki pages touched' section citing both [[modules/backend/transactions]] and [[modules/frontend/transactions]] (or their real names in the wiki) plus [[entities/transaction]]
Ticket includes TypeScript/Prisma code snippets for the new DTO, service method, and controller endpoint
Ticket mentions the atomic balance-sync concern (Prisma $transaction pattern) in Implementation Notes
Ticket includes an Implementation Notes section with warnings about complexity or edge cases (duplicate rows, invalid categories, etc.)
Ticket contains at least 6 Acceptance Criteria covering both backend API behavior and frontend UI
The skill reads wiki pages first rather than scanning budgetwise-api/src/ or budgetwise-ui/src/ as the primary context source
